## Sponsor Meeting Minutes
OCTOBER 29th, 2026 / 2 PM / Zoom and in person, Adele Learning Halls, Room 130

## Attendees
Team: Barzan Mustafa, Clayton Howe, Keyik Annagulyyeva, Oliver Luebcke, Trang Tran, and Vrisheek Venkatesh Goud Panjala
UNL Faculty and Staff: Melanie Kugler-Wright, Kang-il Park, and Ben Ferguson
Sponsors: Alexa Davis, Rachael Whitehair, Nick Arneson, Eric Dinger, and Sarah Starostka
Agenda

## Accomplishments from our last meeting
- Integrated the NRD data layer into the Technical Support Directory map
- Improved the website header based on sponsor preferences from the last meeting
- Converted the Technical Support Directory and Producer Networks maps to ArcGIS
- Reviewed the submission intake form requirements from the sponsors and started work on the form
- Verified that the database matches the sponsors' previous Producer Networks data
- Published the Sprint 2 retrospective and developer documentation on GitHub

## Sprint goal status
- Submission intake form design and mock-up: In progress. Being designed based on Alexa's feedback.
- Enable producer network browsing: In progress. Building the UI so users can search producer networks beside the map.
- Display producer network details: In progress. Network details will show when a user hovers over a producer network on the map.
- Improve mobile usability and reliability: In progress. Ongoing as the other goals are finished.

## Project Roadmap
- The team is in the middle of Sprint 3, continuing work on the mobile view, the ArcGIS maps, data verification and unit testing.
- Release 1.0 will be shown at the release meeting on Thursday, November 5th, when Sprint 3 ends and Sprint 4 begins.
- Faculty requested two roadmap changes:
  - Sprints should end on Thursdays. Change Sprint 3 to October 22nd to November 5th in the heading and the release tag, and roll the Thursday dates through the rest of the semester.
  - Sprint 5 falls over Thanksgiving and Sprint 6 is only one week, so make Sprint 5 a three week sprint ending December 10th.
- A spring semester roadmap needs sponsor approval before Thanksgiving.

## Risk
- API/data structure compatibility
  - Status: Open.
  - Mitigation: use the API field dictionary to map API data to our database structure, and test API responses before implementation.
  - API requirements for the field dictionary are clarified; the final field list is pending.
  - Eric will share the API documentation on Friday, October 30th.
- Delayed release testing (added after the call)
  - Sponsors may not be able to finish testing in time.
  - Mitigation: give sponsors a one week feedback deadline, with the team willing to negotiate a later date if needed.

## Issues
- No new issues were reported.
  - Faculty noted that the API/data structure item reads more like an issue than a risk, since the team already knows about it. If a problem is already known, track it as an issue with a recovery plan, which the team already has.

## Questions
- Field trip
  - The field trip was cancelled due to rain; the team and sponsors had a three hour coffee chat instead.
  - Rescheduled for Monday, November 2nd, at Jason's farm. Backup is Mike Bergen's farm next door, and the backup date is November 9th.
  - Rachael will check with Jason on Friday and Sunday and post an update in the Teams chat on Sunday afternoon.
- How can sponsors and coalition members give feedback on the website?
  - Rachael wants to share the work with the broader coalition for detailed feedback, down to header wording, labels and directory data.
  - Team suggested taking screenshots, adding comments in a doc and posting it in the Teams general channel, tagging the team. The playground link can be used to review the site.
  - Rachael will compile labeled screenshots into a shared online PDF that coalition members can comment on.
- Should the program library include only cost share programs or all programs? (Eric)
  - Nebraska likely has several hundred programs, including carbon, habitat, NRCS and private programs.
  - Rachael: include as many as possible if there is a good way to filter them, using Eric's existing pathways (direct cost share, government, private, carbon focused).
- Should we keep the current filtering or add more?
  - Eric: the API currently returns everything, so many filters are possible. The question is how flexible versus how complicated the filtering should be.
  - Agreed to hold a short design meeting with Eric and Rachael to decide on the filters and data.
- How should payment details be structured? (Eric)
  - Programs pay in very different ways (per acre, per bushel, fixed, annual, multi year), so separate fields do not sort well.
  - Eric's database has a new natural language description of each program's cost share and payments.
  - Agreed to keep it simple: program name, description, payment terms and application deadline, with attributes such as cost share, carbon and nitrogen reduction to sort by.
  - Rachael supported fewer fields so farmers have less to sift through.
- How do we avoid duplicate programs when people submit new ones while Eric's system also adds programs?
  - Eric: the API will have a form listener that feeds submissions into their nomination process, and approved programs reach our program viewer through the API.
  - The team must decide whether to host its own form (full control) or host Eric's form (changes need both sides). To be decided in the design meeting.
  - Outside submissions also help keep Eric's database accurate.
- Is the release meeting on Wednesday, November 4th or Thursday, November 5th?
  - Thursday, November 5th.
- How long do sponsors have to test the release? (Trang)
  - Ask sponsors to test independently from the release meeting through the following week, and negotiate if they cannot.
  - Set an internal last useful date. Feedback much later than a week or two adds little value and can wait until Release 2.
- How do we show who is leading a meeting?
  - Open by saying who is leading and what the meeting is (for example, "Today is our first release meeting").
  - One option: the lead facilitates the whole meeting, introducing each speaker and asking for questions after each part. The team can choose its own style.

## Goals for next week
- Create the submission intake form prototype so sponsors can see and interact with it
- Complete the Producer Networks front end and unit testing
- Test the mobile and browser views and fix bugs
- Prepare for the release meeting on November 5th (release notes, user guide, defect tracker, test outline)
- Review the API documentation and schedule the design meeting with Eric and Rachael
- Draft the spring roadmap for sponsor approval

## Next Steps
- Sprint 3 ends next week and Release 1 is presented at the November 5th meeting.
- Eric will share the API documentation on Friday, October 30th.
- The team will set up a design meeting with Eric and Rachael on filters, data fields and the nomination form.
- Field trip on Monday, November 2nd, weather permitting (backup November 9th).
- After the release, sponsors will test the product independently for about a week and log feedback in the defect tracker.
- The next Sponsor Meeting will be on Thursday, November 5th, from 2PM to ~3PM (room 130 Adele Learning Commons)

## Notes
- Andy suggested connecting the NSAC website with Eric's program data and the spatial decision support tool his group is building for Game and Parks, to reduce friction for producers. He also raised cost share for monitoring tools such as acoustic recording units as a future resource.
- Faculty feedback: the team has a good rapport with engaged sponsors and is on track or ahead. Agenda and slides were sent ahead of time, Trang facilitated well, and the Sprint 2 retrospective was well done (either retrospective format is fine).
- Grading period 2 behaviors are cumulative with period 1 and cover ZenHub, product management, DevOps, releases and risk management.
- Read Melanie's release process prep post in the SD Team channel (October 9th). It lists every expected release step.
- The developer guide on GitHub counts as the technical guide. A user guide for the people using the site is still needed.
- Sponsor testing should come with a high level test outline covering the happy path, edge cases and negative tests, plus a shared defect tracker (for example an Excel sheet in Teams) that sponsors and faculty can access. Review test results at the following meeting.
- Assign a release to all current and future issues in ZenHub. Grading period 1 is over, so this is not needed retroactively.
- ZenHub: in progress stories were last sprint's goals that are not finished. Product backlog items do not need a sprint or release yet; assign them during sprint planning.
- Questions that help the whole team go to Melanie in the SD Team channel; personal matters go in a direct chat.

## Action Items
- Team: Assign a release to all current and future issues in ZenHub.
- Team: Update the roadmap so sprints end on Thursdays (Sprint 3 ends November 5th) and make Sprint 5 a three week sprint ending December 10th.
- Team: Read the release process prep document and prepare release notes for November 5th.
- Team: Create a user guide for Release 1, including a section on sponsor action items.
- Team: Set up a shared defect tracker and a test outline for sponsors.
- Team: Ask sponsors to test from November 5th through the following week, and set a last useful date for feedback.
- Team: Draft the spring roadmap and get sponsor approval before Thanksgiving.
- Team: Let Melanie know if the November 2nd field trip will not happen so she can file insurance for November 9th.
- Oliver Luebcke: Email Eric and Rachael to schedule the design meeting on filters, data fields and the nomination form.
- Eric Dinger: Share the API documentation on Friday, October 30th.
- Rachael Whitehair: Check the weather with Jason and post a field trip update in Teams on Sunday afternoon.
- Melanie Kugler-Wright: Submit the field trip insurance form for November 2nd.
- Rachael Whitehair: Compile labeled screenshots into a shared PDF for coalition feedback.

## Next Meeting Agenda
- Accomplishments from our last meeting
- Sprint goal status
- Project Roadmap
- Issues
- Risks
- Demo
- Questions
- Goals for next week
- Next Steps

## After the call
- Confirmed the roadmap changes: move sprint end dates to Thursdays and extend Sprint 5 to December 10th.
- Spring roadmap: show a rough draft at the release meeting and ask the sponsors whether it meets their expectations.
- Sponsor feedback process: sponsors comment in Figma for designs, and for website pages they put numbered screenshots in a Google Doc. A defect tracker spreadsheet lists each numbered item with its status (fixed or not fixed), so the same problem is not reported twice. Links to all three will go in the user guide.
- Added a new risk, delayed release testing, with a one week feedback deadline as the mitigation.
- Releases only need to be assigned to current and future issues; product backlog stories do not need sprints yet.
- Everyone should look at the cost share issues in ZenHub and assign themselves to ones they can start early.
- Topics for the meeting with Eric and Rachael: the API documentation, filtering, and whether the scope is cost share programs only or all programs. Sponsors seem to prefer basic fields (name, description, deadline) over a payment filter.
- One team member cannot attend the Monday field trip.
